title: Ab initio Green's function theory of superfluid neutron matter
authors: F. Marino, W. G. Jiang, C. Barbieri, G. Colò
abstract: At the low densities encountered in the inner crust of neutron stars, neutron matter becomes superfluid, directly influencing macroscopic phenomena such as star cooling. However, a precise quantitative understanding of this system has been hindered by uncontrolled many-body approximations. In this letter, we exploit the nonperturbative Gorkov algebraic diagrammatic construction method to provide a unified ab initio description of the equation of state and the single-particle spectral functions of homogeneous neutron matter, spanning from the dilute regime to saturation density. We identify clear microscopic signatures of superfluidity in the excitation spectrum and quantify the pairing gaps associated with realistic chiral Hamiltonians, estimating for the first time their sensitivity to the many-body truncation. Our robust handling of both dynamical and pairing correlations paves the way for exploring electroweak processes across the regimes relevant to neutron stars.
summary: This work develops an ab initio Green's function theory to study superfluid neutron matter, crucial for understanding neutron stars. By employing the nonperturbative Gorkov-ADC method, the authors calculate the equation of state and pairing gaps across all relevant densities. The key finding is the quantitative renormalization of the pairing gap when moving beyond simple mean-field approximations.
main_problem: To provide a precise, quantitative understanding of superfluid neutron matter, particularly the pairing gaps, which has been hindered by uncontrolled many-body approximations.
main_result: The Gorkov-ADC method successfully quantifies the pairing gap and equation of state across density regimes, showing that beyond-mean-field corrections renormalize the gap compared to simpler approximations.
method: The study employs the nonperturbative Gorkov algebraic diagrammatic construction (ADC) method within the Green's function formalism to calculate self-energies and spectral functions.
model_or_system: The system is homogeneous neutron matter, relevant to the inner crust of neutron stars, modeled using realistic chiral Hamiltonians and analyzed across varying densities (Fermi momentum $k_F$).
key_observables: Equation of state (EOS), single-particle spectral functions, and the pairing gap ($\Delta$).
important_parameters: Fermi momentum ($k_F$), density, and the comparison between different many-body approximation levels (HFB vs. ADC(3)).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Gorkov formalism and involves approximations like the third-order ADC ($	ext{ADC}(3)$) and renormalization techniques to handle dynamical and pairing correlations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spectral function transition from normal to superfluid regimes, plot the pairing gap ($\Delta$) versus Fermi momentum for various approximations, and compare the energy per particle across different theoretical frameworks.
paper_structure: The paper develops the Gorkov equation framework, compares results from HFB theory to beyond-mean-field theories (ADC(3)), and demonstrates how the pairing gap is renormalized by dynamical correlations, providing a unified description from dilute to saturation density.
why_interesting: While focused on nuclear matter, the use of advanced diagrammatic techniques (like ADC) to calculate pairing gaps and spectral functions in a strongly interacting, superfluid system shares methodological parallels with BCS theory applied to ultracold Fermi gases.
